newsitem.title: FRANCE: HORSE RACING-ASHKALANI UNDERLINES HIS CLASS.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-ASHKALANI UNDERLINES HIS CLASS.

text.p: Ashkalani, the high-class miler owned by the Aga Khan, stamped his authority on the group one Prix du Moulin with an impressive victory at Longchamp on Sunday.
Gerald Mosse rode Ashkalani to a one and a half lengths success over Spinning World, the mount of Cash Asmussen, with Shake The Yoke edged into third place by a short head.
Ashkalani, the 4-5 favourite, was initially held in fourth as Metaphor, acting as pacemaker for Spinning World, set off at a tremendous pace by opening up a big lead.
Inevitably, Metaphor came back to the field and, after Carling briefly held the lead, Mosse galvanised Ashkalani into top gear.
The son of Soviet Star quickened into the lead over a furlong out and quickly sealed the outcome by holding Spinning World, whom he was beating for the third time this year.
Mosse said: "Everything went right for Ashkalani and he was brilliant today. I wouldn't say he was the best miler I have ever ridden, but he is certainly right there at the top of the class."
The Aga Khan said: "He is a lovely horse and the group one Queen Elizabeth II Stakes at Ascot (September 28) could be next on the agenda."
The English track at Ascot remains the only course where Ashkalani has tasted defeat in a six-race career.
Jonathan Pease, trainer of Spinning World, said: "We were beaten by a better horse on the day. Although the horse acts on fast ground, he is best with some cut."
